  "cut_point": "We are asked to evaluate:

$$
\sin 230^\circ \left(1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 170^\circ\right)
$$

---

### Step 1: Simplify $\sin 230^\circ$

We know that:

$$
\sin(230^\circ) = \sin(180^\circ + 50^\circ) = -\sin(50^\circ)
$$

So:

$$
\sin 230^\circ = -\sin 50^\circ
$$

---

### Step 2: Simplify $\tan 170^\circ$

We note that:

$$
170^\circ = 180^\circ - 10^\circ \Rightarrow \tan 170^\circ = -\tan 10^\circ
$$

---

### Step 3: Plug into the expression

$$
\sin 230^\circ (1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 170^\circ) = (-\sin 50^\circ) \left(1 - \sqrt{3}(-\tan 10^\circ)\right)
$$

$$
= -\sin 50^\circ \left(1 + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ\right)
$$

---

### Step 4: Evaluate $\sin 50^\circ$ and $\tan 10^\circ$

It is known that:

- $\sin 50^\circ \approx 0.7660$
- $\tan 10^\circ \approx 0.1763$

So:

$$
-\sin 50^\circ \left(1 + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ\right) \approx -0.7660 \left(1 + 1.732 \times 0.1763\right)
$$

$$
\approx -0.7660 \left(1 + 0.305\right) = -0.7660 \times 1.305 \approx -0.997
$$",
  "reflection": {
    "verified_state": [
      "\sin 230^\circ = \sin(180^\circ + 50^\circ) = -\sin 50^\circ",
      "\tan 170^\circ = \tan(180^\circ - 10^\circ) = -\tan 10^\circ",
      "The expression simplifies exactly to \(-\sin 50^\circ(1+\sqrt3\tan 10^\circ)\)",
      "Using decimal approximations gives \(-\sin 50^\circ(1+\sqrt3\tan 10^\circ) \approx -0.7660(1+1.732\times0.1763)\)"
    ],
    "error_step": "$$
\approx -0.7660 \left(1 + 0.305\right) = -0.7660 \times 1.305 \approx -0.997
$$",
    "error_reason": "The multiplication is incorrect: \(-0.7660 \times 1.305 \approx -0.9996\), not \(-0.997\). More fundamentally, decimal approximations cannot establish the exact value \(-1\).",
    "new_direction": "Do not use decimal approximations; instead simplify \(-\sin 50^\circ(1+\sqrt3\tan 10^\circ)\) exactly using trigonometric identities to obtain \(-1\)."
  }

annotation.cut_point:
We are asked to evaluate:

$$
\sin 230^\circ \left(1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 170^\circ\right)
$$

---

### Step 1: Simplify $\sin 230^\circ$

We know that:

$$
\sin(230^\circ) = \sin(180^\circ + 50^\circ) = -\sin(50^\circ)
$$

So:

$$
\sin 230^\circ = -\sin 50^\circ
$$

---

### Step 2: Simplify $\tan 170^\circ$

We note that:

$$
170^\circ = 180^\circ - 10^\circ \Rightarrow \tan 170^\circ = -\tan 10^\circ
$$

---

### Step 3: Plug into the expression

$$
\sin 230^\circ (1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 170^\circ) = (-\sin 50^\circ) \left(1 - \sqrt{3}(-\tan 10^\circ)\right)
$$

$$
= -\sin 50^\circ \left(1 + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ\right)
$$

---

### Step 4: Evaluate $\sin 50^\circ$ and $\tan 10^\circ$

It is known that:

- $\sin 50^\circ \approx 0.7660$
- $\tan 10^\circ \approx 0.1763$

So:

$$
-\sin 50^\circ \left(1 + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ\right) \approx -0.7660 \left(1 + 1.732 \times 0.1763\right)
$$

$$
\approx -0.7660 \left(1 + 0.305\right) = -0.7660 \times 1.305 \approx -0.997
$$

reflection.error_reason: The multiplication is incorrect: \(-0.7660 \times 1.305 \approx -0.9996\), not \(-0.997\). More fundamentally, decimal approximations cannot establish the exact value \(-1\).
reflection.new_direction: Do not use decimal approximations; instead simplify \(-\sin 50^\circ(1+\sqrt3\tan 10^\circ)\) exactly using trigonometric identities to obtain \(-1\).
